description:
## Problem
After #4304, `benchbox/validation/bundle.py` (around the non-standard-scale branch) returns with a warning for an off-list scale before it checks the recorded `compliance_class`, so any string, including garbage, passes for those bundles.

## Change
Check the recorded class against the allowed set {official, unofficial_nonstandard, unofficial_subscale} (a per-benchmark enum exists only for tpch and tpcds) (approved by the owner on 2026-11-20) before the early return; keep the off-list bundle accepted and unranked as #4304 intended.

## Decision gates
None. Do not change which bundles are ranked.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test bundle at an off-list scale with `compliance_class` set to an unknown string fails validation; the 13 ClickBench bundles made unranked by #4304 still validate; `results-data/validate_corpus.py` reports the same counts as before on the committed corpus.

## Additions from the item review
- Rubric addition: attach `results-data/validate_corpus.py` output from before and after the change, with the diff.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
